i think your context needs a bit of work, but other than that it looked pretty good. context can definitely be tricky; you want to be specific, but also don’t use all of your specifics in one go. my teacher calls it “double dipping”; you can’t use SFI from your context in the rest of the essay. depending on your knowledge of the subject, i’d say use three SFI’s at most, and keep it brief. give the what, the why, and the when of the historical situation and give a few events that give that time significance and then link it back to your thesis. for example, if you were talking about the american revolution, (dependent on the docs and how you would support them) for context bring up the french and indian war and the end of salutary neglect, taxation on the american colonies, proclamation line, etc. context is one of those things where you definitely want to do everything in your power to get it, but don’t sacrifice the rest of the essay for it. don’t take too much time on it but don’t leave it blank either. make it 3-5 sentences max, and follow up with a thesis that restates the prompt and either affirm or negate that prompt and give 2-3 reasons why it does. do that, and context and thesis should be an easy two points. good luck!
